formal_rules: CanDelete(D, t) <=> AuthorizedCleanup(D, t) and IdentityVerified(D) and Users(D) == 0 and NoProtectedDependency(D)
Undo(m) => Authorized(m, t) and Prepared(m, t) and IdentityVerified(m) and CausalEvidence(m) and NoExternalHarm(m)

prohibitions.no_name_inference: name(r) == expected_name does NOT imply Owned(r, t). Object, constraint, collection, or datablock names in Blender are mutable strings and prone to external collision.
prohibitions.no_snapshot_diff_inference: r not in Snapshot does NOT imply Owned(r, t). Resources absent from initial snapshot may belong to external pipelines or user interactions; differential deletion is strictly prohibited.
prohibitions.no_raw_pointer_alone_inference: as_pointer(r) == saved_ptr does NOT imply AliveVerified(r). The underlying C allocator can reuse virtual addresses after memory destruction; pointer equality must be combined with active Python wrapper liveness (no ReferenceError), original reference identity, and data collection inclusion.
prohibitions.no_zero_users_deletion_inference: Users(D) == 0 does NOT imply AuthorizedCleanup(D, t). Zero user count only proves the DataBlock currently has no active user references; it never proves the transaction holds deletion authority over D.
prohibitions.no_object_to_datablock_authority_inherit: Ownership or doomed/stashed deletion authority over an Object NEVER automatically transfers to or grants deletion authority over its bound DataBlock (obj.data).

Object.ownership_criteria: Only objects registered upon creation in active_tx.created_controller_objects or explicitly stashed with proven prior rig ownership in active_tx.stashed_objects.
Object.mutation_authority: Only the active transaction in ACTIVE state is permitted to modify controller numeric transforms (location, rotation_*, scale via Layer 4) or restore them in ROLLING_BACK (via Layer 5). Object relationship references (Object.parent, matrix_parent_inverse parent binding, Collection membership) may ONLY be mutated or restored via Layer 3 Authorized Resource Operations with Layer 2 7-state relationship logging.
Object.deletion_authority: Rollback permits deleting only active_tx.created_controller_objects with verified identity (live reference + pointer + bpy.data.objects inclusion) via Layer 3. Post-commit cleanup permits deleting only authorized stashed doomed objects via Layer 3.
Object.death_detection: ReferenceError on attribute access, pointer divergence, or absence from bpy.data.objects.

Constraint.ownership_criteria: Only constraints registered upon creation in active_tx.created_constraints or explicitly stashed in active_tx.stashed_constraints.
Constraint.mutation_authority: In ACTIVE state, Layer 4 is permitted to update numeric parameters (influence, pole_angle, chain_count, use_stretch); in ROLLING_BACK, Layer 5 restores numeric parameters. Constraint relationship references (Constraint.target, Constraint.pole_target, subtarget, pole_subtarget) may ONLY be mutated or restored via Layer 3 Authorized Resource Operations with Layer 2 7-state relationship logging.
Constraint.deletion_authority: Rollback permits removing only active_tx.created_constraints matching registered bone, reference, and pointer via Layer 3. Post-commit cleanup permits removing authorized stashed doomed constraints via Layer 3.
Constraint.death_detection: ReferenceError on access, pointer divergence, or absence from pose_bone.constraints.

Collection.ownership_criteria: Only collections created by active transaction and registered in active_tx.created_collections.
Collection.mutation_authority: Collection object membership (objects.link/unlink) and child hierarchy links (children.link/unlink) may ONLY be modified in ACTIVE or restored in ROLLING_BACK via Layer 3 Authorized Resource Operations with Layer 2 7-state relationship logging.
Collection.deletion_authority: Rollback permits deleting only registered created collections that contain zero external members and zero external child collections via Layer 3.
Collection.death_detection: ReferenceError, pointer mismatch, or absence from bpy.data.collections.

DataBlock.formal_deletion_predicate: CanDelete(D, t) <=> AuthorizedCleanup(D, t) and IdentityVerified(D) and Users(D) == 0 and NoProtectedDependency(D)

TYPE_A_TX_CREATED.description: DataBlock allocated and explicitly registered by the current transaction in active_tx.created_datablocks.
TYPE_A_TX_CREATED.deletion_policy: Transaction holds explicit creation authority. Permitted to delete during rollback or cleanup if and only if IdentityVerified(D) and Users(D) == 0 and NoProtectedDependency(D).

TYPE_B_PRE_EXISTING.description: DataBlock that existed prior to transaction entry (even if bound to an Object modified or deleted by the transaction).
TYPE_B_PRE_EXISTING.deletion_policy: Transaction does NOT acquire deletion authority merely because an associated Object was deleted or marked doomed. Deletion is forbidden unless an independent, explicit, provenance-verified DataBlock cleanup authorization record exists for D. Without such independent grant, D must be preserved as PRESERVED_NO_DELETE_AUTHORITY.

TYPE_C_EXTERNAL_OR_UNPROVEN.description: DataBlock created externally or whose provenance/authorization cannot be proven.
TYPE_C_EXTERNAL_OR_UNPROVEN.deletion_policy: Strictly FORBIDDEN to delete under any circumstances, even if Users(D) == 0, absent from snapshot, or sharing a name with a doomed Object.

required_fields.resource_kind: String identifier of Blender datablock collection (e.g., 'Mesh', 'Curve', 'Armature').
required_fields.original_reference: Live Python RNA wrapper reference to the DataBlock captured at registration.
required_fields.original_pointer: Integer C-memory address (D.as_pointer()) captured at registration.
required_fields.authorization_source: Explicit caller/operation that granted DataBlock-specific cleanup authority (e.g., 'Layer3.allocate_internal_datablock' or explicit retirement contract; never implicit inheritance from Object deletion).
required_fields.authorized_transaction: Unique transaction ID (tx_id) to which the authorization is bound.

governance_rules.who_grants_authority: Layer 3 Resource Operations upon direct allocation within active transaction (Type A), or Layer 4 Business API supplying an explicit, verifiable prior-ownership retirement record registered into Layer 2 before object detachment (Type B).
governance_rules.validity_verification: Authorization is valid only if authorized_transaction matches the executing transaction (or its registered pending cleanup context), authorization_scope == 'PHYSICAL_DELETE_IF_ZERO_USERS', and provenance is TYPE_A or TYPE_B_PRE_EXISTING_EXPLICIT_GRANT.
governance_rules.identity_verification: original_reference must not raise ReferenceError, original_reference.as_pointer() == original_pointer, and original_reference must exist in the corresponding bpy.data collection.
governance_rules.reference_and_dependency_verification: D.users == 0, D.use_fake_user is False, D.library is None, and no external object, modifier, constraint, or driver references D.
governance_rules.unauthorized_handling: If an Object is legally deleted/cleaned but its former DataBlock lacks valid PHYSICAL_DELETE_IF_ZERO_USERS authorization, Layer 6 / Layer 3 MUST preserve the DataBlock and record status 'PRESERVED_NO_DELETE_AUTHORITY'. This is a valid, terminal resource-protection outcome and MUST NOT trigger CLEANUP_PENDING or retry loops.
governance_rules.obligatory_cleanup_failure_handling: If a DataBlock possesses valid PHYSICAL_DELETE_IF_ZERO_USERS authorization (obligatory cleanup) but cannot be deleted (e.g., unexpected active user reference or RNA removal error), Layer 6 records a cleanup failure and returns CLEANUP_INCOMPLETE / CLEANUP_FAILED to Layer 1 Coordinator, which enforces the CLEANUP_PENDING contract.

DataBlock.death_detection: ReferenceError on access, pointer mismatch against original_pointer, or absence from corresponding bpy.data collection.

external_relationship_conflict_policy.description: Handling scenario where a transaction-created entity is subsequently referenced by external systems.
policy_rules: Step 1: Verify entity's original ownership record in active_tx.
Step 2: Inspect all active live relationships (parenting, collection memberships, constraint targets, modifier targets).
Step 3: Distinguish relationships registered by this transaction from external relationships.
Step 4: If an external system has attached to the transaction-created entity and the external relationship cannot be safely undone, the transaction is FORBIDDEN from destroying the entity blindly.

Step 5: Rollback must halt, flag OWNERSHIP_CONFLICT / RECOVERY_UNCERTAIN, leave the entity intact, and report recovery failure to Layer 1 Coordinator to prevent cascading destruction of external scene graph.

unknown_ownership_policy.behavior: Any entity, DataBlock, or relationship whose provenance cannot be proven to belong to the active transaction and was not recorded with explicit authority is treated as OWNERSHIP_UNPROVEN. Destructive operations (delete, unlink, overwrite) are strictly rejected.

PRE_EXISTING_ORIGINAL.description: Relationships that existed prior to transaction entry (e.g., character collection already linked to master/scene collection, pre-existing bone constraints).
PRE_EXISTING_ORIGINAL.rollback_rule: Strictly protected. If the transaction executes a duplicate link or re-bind, it transitions to NO_EFFECT and NEVER acquires revocation or unlinking rights. Original links must remain intact upon rollback.

TX_ADDED.description: Relationships newly established by the active transaction (e.g. newly created controller linked to Character collection).
TX_ADDED.rollback_rule: Subject to rollback. Reverted by unlinking or removal upon rollback (transitioning log to REVERTED) ONLY IF supported by authorized PREPARED record, valid identity, proven causal evidence, and zero external harm.

TX_UNLINKED_ORIGINAL.description: Pre-existing original relationships explicitly detached or unlinked by the transaction during business execution.
TX_UNLINKED_ORIGINAL.rollback_rule: Must be re-linked / restored to original state during rollback (transitioning log to REVERTED), preserving original target and relative ordering.

EXTERNAL_ADDED.description: Relationships created by external scripts, operators, or user interaction during or after transaction start.
EXTERNAL_ADDED.rollback_rule: Strictly immune to rollback destruction. Transaction is FORBIDDEN from unlinking or deleting external relationships.

OWNERSHIP_UNKNOWN.description: Relationships whose origin, authorization, or causal history cannot be conclusively proven.
OWNERSHIP_UNKNOWN.rollback_rule: Treated as OWNERSHIP_UNPROVEN. Rollback halts destructive action on this relationship, leaves it untouched, transitions relationship log to RECOVERY_UNCERTAIN, and reports verification failure.

f1_relationship_atomicity.operation_log_state_notes: These 7 states belong exclusively to the Relationship Operation Log State Machine tracked in active_tx.prepared_relationship_mutations. They are NOT transaction lifecycle states. The Transaction Lifecycle State Machine remains strictly composed of 9 states. No 8th relationship log state or 10th transaction lifecycle state is permitted.

relationship_log_state_definitions.PREPARED: Authorization verified and intent record created in transaction memory before invoking any Blender C-API relationship mutation.
relationship_log_state_definitions.APPLYING: Authorized Blender C-API relationship operation has been invoked; execution is in progress and may succeed, partially apply, or raise an error.
relationship_log_state_definitions.APPLIED_VERIFIED: Post-call RNA inspection confirmed the expected relationship mutation took effect in live Blender data; awaiting high-level business step confirmation.
relationship_log_state_definitions.CONFIRMED: Relationship operation is confirmed complete within the active business step. Serves as a valid completion state when the transaction commits, but remains subject to authorized undo (CONFIRMED -> REVERTED / RECOVERY_UNCERTAIN) if the enclosing transaction rolls back.
relationship_log_state_definitions.NO_EFFECT: Terminal log state proving zero relationship modification requiring undo occurred (e.g., aborted at PREPARED before APPLYING; APPLYING raised an error and live RNA inspection proved zero side effect; or operation was a no-op on a PRE_EXISTING_ORIGINAL relationship).
relationship_log_state_definitions.REVERTED: Terminal rollback log state proving that a relationship modification caused by this transaction operation has been legally undone and post-undo verification confirmed restoration of the prior relationship state.
relationship_log_state_definitions.RECOVERY_UNCERTAIN: Terminal error log state indicating provenance, live physical effect, or safe undo preconditions cannot be proven; speculative unlinking/deletion is forbidden and scene state is preserved.

Transaction aborts before APPLYING is invoked, or pre-check determines relationship is already PRE_EXISTING_ORIGINAL requiring no mutation.

Blender C-API call fails and live RNA topology is unreadable, corrupted, or exhibits unprovable external interference.
Layer 3 / Layer 4 completes post-mutation registration and confirms the operation within the active transaction.
Transaction enters ROLLING_BACK before confirmation; Layer 5 / Layer 3 legally undoes the verified mutation and confirms restoration.
Transaction enters ROLLING_BACK before confirmation, but undo fails, identity is invalidated, or external conflict prevents safe reversal.
Enclosing transaction enters ROLLING_BACK after operation confirmation; Layer 5 / Layer 3 legally undoes the mutation per ownership contract and verifies restoration.
Enclosing transaction enters ROLLING_BACK after operation confirmation, but undo fails or external dependency conflict prevents safe reversal.

relationship_log_terminal_states.rollback_verification_coupling: During ROLLING_BACK, every log record in APPLIED_VERIFIED or CONFIRMED must resolve to REVERTED (or NO_EFFECT if proven pre-existing). Any record remaining in APPLIED_VERIFIED, CONFIRMED, or transitioning to RECOVERY_UNCERTAIN causes Layer 5 rollback verification to fail, triggering Layer 1 transition to FAILED (FAILED-B / FAILED-C).

formal_rollback_principle.theorem: Undo(m) => Authorized(m, t) and Prepared(m, t) and IdentityVerified(m) and CausalEvidence(m) and NoExternalHarm(m)
axioms: 1. Active Transaction Authorization: Mutation m must have been explicitly authorized under the active transaction context t.
2. Prepare Record Existence: A valid PREPARED log entry must exist in active_tx.prepared_relationship_mutations before any Blender C-API mutation was executed.
3. Valid Resource Identity: Source and destination RNA entities must remain alive and pointer/reference-verified (no stale pointer reuse, no ReferenceError).

4. Causal Evidence Proven: Physical inspection of live scene topology must prove the observed relationship modification was directly produced by this transaction operation (APPLIED_VERIFIED or CONFIRMED), not PRE_EXISTING_ORIGINAL or EXTERNAL_ADDED.
5. Zero External Harm Risk: Undoing the relationship mutation must carry zero risk of breaking external scene graph dependencies.

6. Incomplete CONFIRM does NOT imply mutation did not occur: An operation in APPLYING or APPLIED_VERIFIED must be evaluated against live RNA state and reverted to REVERTED if causal evidence is proven.

7. CONFIRMED is NOT permanently irreversible prior to transaction commit: When the enclosing transaction rolls back, CONFIRMED operations with TX_ADDED or TX_UNLINKED_ORIGINAL provenance must be undone and transitioned to REVERTED.
8. Prohibition of Name or Differential Inference: Relationship ownership cannot be inferred from object names or snapshot set difference.
9. Duplicate Link No Revocation: For PRE_EXISTING_ORIGINAL, repeated link operations transition to NO_EFFECT and never claim ownership or unlinking rights.
10. Site Preservation on Uncertainty: For unprovable changes, preserve scene site, transition log to RECOVERY_UNCERTAIN, and fail rollback verification.

phase_prepare.description: Pre-flight and register intent before mutating Blender relationship state.
actions: Verify identity of source and target entities (ReferenceError, reference identity, and pointer check).
Verify mutation authorization under current transaction context.
Check whether relationship already exists in live scene; if PRE_EXISTING_ORIGINAL and operation is link, record PREPARED and immediately transition to NO_EFFECT without mutating Blender.
Otherwise record mutation intent in active_tx.prepared_relationship_mutations with unique op_id, source reference/pointer, target reference/pointer, category, and initial state PREPARED.
phase_prepare.on_failure: If preparation fails before C-API call, any created log entry transitions to NO_EFFECT and ZERO Blender relationships are modified.

phase_apply.description: Execute authorized relationship mutation in Blender C-API and verify immediate live effect.
actions: Transition log status from PREPARED to APPLYING.
Execute specific relationship API (col.objects.link, col.children.link, obj.parent = ..., con.target = ...).
Inspect RNA structure immediately post-call: if target mutation is present and verified, transition log status to APPLIED_VERIFIED.
phase_apply.on_exception: Inspect live RNA relationship state against PREPARED record: if zero change occurred in Blender, transition log to NO_EFFECT; if change partially applied and is verified, transition to APPLIED_VERIFIED for subsequent rollback; if live state is ambiguous or corrupted, transition to RECOVERY_UNCERTAIN.

phase_confirm.description: Verify post-mutation state and mark operation confirmed in transaction memory.
actions: Confirm live topology matches expected target relationship.
Transition mutation record in active_tx from APPLIED_VERIFIED to CONFIRMED.

phase_failure_recovery.description: Rollback behavior when apply, confirm, or subsequent business operations fail.
rules: Inspect all relationship mutation records in active_tx.
Records in NO_EFFECT require zero undo action.
Records in PREPARED (never applied) transition to NO_EFFECT.
Records in APPLYING are first resolved to NO_EFFECT, APPLIED_VERIFIED, or RECOVERY_UNCERTAIN by live inspection.
Records in APPLIED_VERIFIED or CONFIRMED are undone ONLY if Undo(m) preconditions hold; upon verified restoration, transition record to REVERTED.
If Undo(m) preconditions fail or post-undo check fails, preserve scene site and transition record to RECOVERY_UNCERTAIN.

Layer1_TransactionCoordinator.state_owner: Global _ACTIVE_TRANSACTION_STACK control, Sole Authority for all 9 Transaction Lifecycle State Machine Transitions and Gate Deregistration Decisions

taxonomy.CALL: Downward invocation dependency where a higher layer calls a function in a lower layer. Participates in DAG topological sorting.
taxonomy.RESULT: Upward operation outcome returned via function return value along the Python call stack (e.g., CleanupOutcome, VerificationResult, GateResult). Does NOT represent an invocation dependency and does NOT participate in DAG topological sorting.
taxonomy.STATE_READ: Read-only query of passive data structures in Layer 2 Registry.
taxonomy.STATE_WRITE: Authorized update of records, lifecycle states, or gate indices in Layer 2 Registry. Lifecycle state and gate registration/deregistration writes are restricted exclusively to Layer 1 Coordinator.
taxonomy.PROTECTION: Read-only ownership and provenance boundary inspection where an active transaction layer (Source: Layer 3 / Layer 5 / Layer 6) inspects and protects external or unproven resources (Target: External Scene Resources & Unproven DataBlocks) from unauthorized modification or deletion.

f2_directed_dependency_graph.cycle_elimination_proof: The dependency graph of invocation calls (CALL edges) is a strict Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) with topological ordering: WBC -> Layer 4 -> Layer 1 -> Layer 5 -> Layer 6 -> Layer 3 -> Layer 2. Layer 2 is a pure passive store with zero outgoing calls. Layer 6 has zero call dependencies on Layer 1 and is forbidden from independently deregistering gates in Layer 2. Layer 6 returns CleanupOutcome via stack return (RESULT) to Layer 1, and Layer 1 alone commands Layer 2 to update lifecycle state and clear or retain the CLEANUP_PENDING gate.

f2_state_transition_authority.sole_authority: Layer 1 Transaction Coordinator is the SOLE decision maker for all 9 transaction lifecycle state transitions and all admission gate registrations/deregistrations.
f2_state_transition_authority.state_machine_separation_rule: The 9 Transaction Lifecycle States (managed by Layer 1) and the 7 Relationship Operation Log States (managed by Layer 3/5 in Layer 2 logs) are strictly separate state machines and must never be conflated.

CREATED.condition: Coordinator verifies session identity and admission gate, then transitions to SNAPSHOTTING. If pre-snapshot initialization fails with zero writes, transitions to FAILED (classified as FAILED-A).

SNAPSHOTTING.condition: Layer 5 completes read-only baseline snapshot (transitions to ACTIVE). If snapshot read fails before any business write, Coordinator transitions transaction to FAILED (classified as FAILED-A if zero writes and scene uncorrupted, or FAILED-C/D if pre-existing structural corruption/death is detected).

ACTIVE.condition: Business logic finishes without error and rollback_only is False (COMMITTING), or catches runtime exception / detects rollback_only == True (ROLLING_BACK).

COMMITTING.condition: Phase 1 depsgraph update and commit preparation pass (crosses irreversible commit line to COMMITTED) or fail (ROLLING_BACK).

COMMITTED.condition: Irreversible commit crossed. Ordinary rollback FORBIDDEN. Layer 1 invokes Layer 6 cleanup. If Layer 6 returns CLEANUP_SUCCESS (including items marked PRESERVED_NO_DELETE_AUTHORITY), transaction remains COMMITTED and gate is clear. If Layer 6 returns CLEANUP_INCOMPLETE or CLEANUP_FAILED for obligatory cleanup items, Coordinator transitions state to CLEANUP_PENDING and registers gate in Layer 2.

ROLLING_BACK.condition: Layer 5 rollback and full-field verification succeed 100% with all modified relationship logs resolved to REVERTED or NO_EFFECT (ROLLED_BACK). If rollback execution fails (FAILED-B), verification detects diff/RECOVERY_UNCERTAIN (FAILED-C), or Armature died (FAILED-D), Coordinator transitions to FAILED and instructs Layer 2 to record persistent session isolation/tombstone.

ROLLED_BACK.condition: Terminal state for cleanly aborted transaction. Baseline state 100% verified restored. Coordinator pops transaction and re-raises original business exception.

CLEANUP_PENDING.condition: Registered by Coordinator in Layer 2 _PENDING_ARM_RIG_CLEANUPS. Blocks new write transactions on the same Armature session identity. Transitions to COMMITTED ONLY when Coordinator invokes Layer 6 retry, receives CLEANUP_SUCCESS, and explicitly authorizes Layer 2 to deregister the pending gate.

FAILED.condition: Terminal transaction state. Never transitions to COMMITTED. Coordinator classifies failure into FAILED-A, FAILED-B, FAILED-C, or FAILED-D to govern Armature session isolation.

f2_state_transition_authority.retry_cleanup_flow: 1. External Caller invokes Coordinator (_dispatch_retry_cleanup) -> 2. Coordinator calls Layer 6 (retry_cleanup) -> 3. Layer 6 executes authorized resource cleanup via Layer 3 and updates item progress in Layer 2 -> 4. Layer 6 returns CleanupOutcome (CLEANUP_SUCCESS | CLEANUP_INCOMPLETE | CLEANUP_FAILED) to Coordinator -> 5. Coordinator evaluates outcome -> 6. If and only if CLEANUP_SUCCESS, Coordinator authorizes Layer 2 Registry -> 7. Layer 2 updates transaction state to COMMITTED and removes Armature from _PENDING_ARM_RIG_CLEANUPS.

nested_transaction_rollback_only_contrac.description: Handling nested transactions on the same Armature.
contract_rules: 1. Inner transaction invocation reuses outer transaction context (stack depth remains 1, single baseline snapshot).
2. If an inner operation raises an exception or fails preflight, even if caught by caller business try/except blocks, it invokes outer_tx.mark_rollback_only(reason).
3. When the outer block exits and attempts to commit, Layer 1 Coordinator checks tx.rollback_only.
4. If tx.rollback_only is True, normal commit is REJECTED; Coordinator forces transition to ROLLING_BACK.
5. Silent commit after inner failure is structurally impossible.

isolation_scope_boundary.supported_scope: In-memory Python session within the active Blender process.
isolation_scope_boundary.out_of_scope_boundary: Cross-process restarts or bpy.ops.wm.open_mainfile() scene reloads reset the Python interpreter memory and constitute an independent persistence boundary (tracked in ARCH-ISSUE-03). The architecture does NOT falsely claim that Python memory structures survive process termination.
isolation_scope_boundary.blender_object_property_constraint: Modifying Blender object custom properties (e.g., arm['uuid']) to store session identity is FORBIDDEN in this phase to preserve zero-mutation snapshot invariants.

fields.registry_session_id: Unique UUID4 string allocated by Layer 2 Registry in Python memory when the Armature instance is first registered in the session.
fields.original_blender_ref: Direct Python RNA reference to the bpy.types.Object armature instance.
fields.in_live_blender_collection: Boolean confirming object is present in bpy.data.objects.values() and scene collection hierarchy.
fields.tombstone_record: Optional diagnostic dictionary populated when liveness_status becomes INVALIDATED_DEAD.

session_identity_model.identity_matching_rule: An incoming Armature 'arm' matches an active ArmatureSessionIdentityRecord if and only if: (1) record.original_blender_ref does not raise ReferenceError, (2) arm == record.original_blender_ref, (3) arm.as_pointer() == record.registration_pointer, and (4) arm is present in bpy.data.objects.values(). Name equality is NEVER used for identity matching.
session_identity_model.pointer_reuse_and_new_armature_protectio: If the original Armature is destroyed in Blender, its record transitions to TOMBSTONED_FAILED_D (liveness_status = INVALIDATED_DEAD). If Blender subsequently allocates a new Armature object that reuses the same C memory pointer or shares the same name, liveness/reference verification detects that the original record is already dead/tombstoned. The new Armature is assigned a fresh registry_session_id: (a) the dead object's tombstone is NOT cleared and the new object is NEVER treated as a recovery of the dead object; (b) the dead object's tombstone does NOT falsely block the legitimate new Armature from executing transactions.

FAILED_A_PRE_WRITE.description: Failure occurring prior to entering ACTIVE (during CREATED or read-only SNAPSHOTTING) with proven zero managed writes.
zero_write_proof_conditions: created_controller_objects, created_constraints, created_collections, stashed_*, and prepared_relationship_mutations are all empty.
No external state corruption occurred during read.
FAILED_A_PRE_WRITE.isolation_policy: The transaction terminates in FAILED state, but if zero managed writes are proven and the Armature structure is intact, Layer 1 Coordinator does NOT place the Armature into persistent FAILED isolation. Subsequent independent transactions may apply for admission. Transaction failure is not conflated with Armature corruption.

FAILED_B_ROLLBACK_EXEC_ERROR.description: Failure occurring during ROLLING_BACK execution (e.g., exception during property restoration, OWNERSHIP_CONFLICT, or relationship log entering RECOVERY_UNCERTAIN).
FAILED_B_ROLLBACK_EXEC_ERROR.isolation_policy: Mandatory persistent session isolation (isolation_state = ISOLATED_FAILED_B). All new write transactions on this Armature session identity are rejected.

FAILED_C_VERIFY_MISMATCH.description: Rollback execution finished, but Layer 5 _verify_arm_rig_state_restored detected missing original resource identity, property diff > 1e-5, or un-reverted relationship mutation.
FAILED_C_VERIFY_MISMATCH.isolation_policy: Mandatory persistent session isolation (isolation_state = ISOLATED_FAILED_C). All new write transactions on this Armature session identity are rejected. Cannot be cleared by same-name substitute resources.

FAILED_D_IDENTITY_INVALIDATED.description: Original Armature RNA object became invalid/destroyed (ReferenceError or removed from bpy.data.objects) during transaction, rollback, or while isolated.
FAILED_D_IDENTITY_INVALIDATED.isolation_policy: Record transitions to TOMBSTONED_FAILED_D. Original identity is permanently dead; cannot be cleared by same-name new objects or pointer reuse, while legitimate new Armature identities are not falsely blocked.

case_1_trusted_snapshot_exists.applicable_to: ISOLATED_FAILED_B or ISOLATED_FAILED_C where baseline snapshot was completely captured and verified immutable.
requirements: All original sub-resources in snapshot pass identity verification (live reference + pointer).
Zero relationship logs remain in RECOVERY_UNCERTAIN or un-reverted TX_ADDED / TX_UNLINKED_ORIGINAL states.

case_2_no_trusted_snapshot_exists.applicable_to: Isolation where snapshot capture was incomplete or untrusted due to concurrent structural anomaly.
requirements: Fabricating or synthesizing a fake snapshot is strictly FORBIDDEN.

Layer 5 executes independent Structural Integrity & Invariant Verification: confirms Armature bone hierarchy is intact, controller/constraint bindings are either 100% clean uninitialized state or 100% valid conformal rig state, and zero orphan transaction artifacts exist.
If independent structural proof is insufficient, isolation MUST remain active.
New objects are NEVER accepted as recovery of the dead Armature.

Handled exclusively via Authorized Tombstone Retirement (retire_dead_armature_tombstone): Layer 5 verifies original RNA object is permanently absent from bpy.data.objects and all transaction-owned orphan artifacts bound to the failed tx_id have been cleaned or accounted for.
Coordinator transitions record from TOMBSTONED_FAILED_D to ARCHIVED_RETIRED in audit log.

deisolation_authority_and_governance.no_imaginary_tokens_rule: Architecture does NOT assume external cryptographic tokens or imaginary key management systems. Authority is enforced through strict architectural separation of verification and state decision roles.
roles_and_workflow: 1. Applicant (Caller): Upper recovery handler invokes Layer 1 Coordinator API request_armature_deisolation(arm, recovery_evidence_context) or retire_dead_armature_tombstone(registry_session_id).

2. Evidence Verifier (Layer 5): Coordinator dispatches Layer 5 verify_armature_deisolation_evidence(), which inspects live Blender state against the category-specific contract (Case 1, Case 2, or Case 3) and returns an immutable DeisolationVerificationReport.

3. Approver & State Decision Authority (Layer 1 Coordinator): Inspects DeisolationVerificationReport. Layer 1 Coordinator is the SOLE authority permitted to approve de-isolation. If report.verified is True, Coordinator issues explicit de-isolation instruction to Layer 2.

4. Registry & Audit Trail (Layer 2): Upon Coordinator authorization, Layer 2 updates isolation_state to NONE (or ARCHIVED_RETIRED for Case 3) and appends an immutable DeisolationAuditEntry (timestamp, registry_session_id, failure_category, verification_report, coordinator_decision) to _DEISOLATION_AUDIT_LOG.

5. Rejection Retention: If verification fails, Coordinator rejects the request, Layer 2 retains isolation_state unchanged, records the rejected attempt in _DEISOLATION_AUDIT_LOG, and raises RuntimeError.

distinction_from_cleanup_pending.CLEANUP_PENDING: Business logic committed; post-commit cleanup of obligatory doomed resources incomplete. Recoverable via controlled Layer 1 -> Layer 6 retry_pending_arm_rig_cleanup.
distinction_from_cleanup_pending.FAILED: Transaction or recovery failed safely to complete. Normal Cleanup Retry NEVER clears FAILED isolation. FAILED NEVER transitions to COMMITTED.

CONTRACT-01.name: Input Validation & Pre-Write Preflight
CONTRACT-01.invariant: All parameters (side, world_xyz, rotation, pole, influence, clamp_reach) and parent transform domains must be pre-validated before any scene mutation. Zero scene writes on rejection.
CONTRACT-01.failure_condition: Non-finite values, out-of-range influence, bad side string, or singular non-invertible parent matrix.
CONTRACT-01.exception_propagation: Immediate TypeError or ValueError; transaction is not entered.

CONTRACT-02.name: Same-Armature Nested Transaction & Failure Propagation
CONTRACT-02.invariant: Re-entrant transaction requests on same Armature session identity reuse active context; stack depth remains 1; inner failure marks transaction rollback-only via explicit reporting path.
CONTRACT-02.failure_condition: Cross-armature nesting requested, or inner failure suppressed by caller.
CONTRACT-02.exception_propagation: Cross-armature raises RuntimeError; suppressed inner failure triggers forced rollback on outer commit.
CONTRACT-02.recovery_responsibility: Outermost Layer 1 Coordinator executes full rollback.

CONTRACT-03.name: Controller & Created DataBlock Provenance Registration
CONTRACT-03.invariant: New controller Empty and any Type A transaction-allocated DataBlock must be registered in active_tx with explicit provenance and pointer/reference identity immediately upon creation and before collection linkage. Rollback deletes strictly registered transaction-created resources.
CONTRACT-03.failure_condition: Creation failure, duplicate registration, or collection link failure.
CONTRACT-03.exception_propagation: Operational exception bubbles to Layer 1, triggering rollback.
CONTRACT-03.recovery_responsibility: Layer 5 deletes registered controller and Type A DataBlock (satisfying CanDelete(D,t)) via Layer 3.

CONTRACT-04.name: Relationship Mutation 7-State Log & Evidence-Based Rollback
CONTRACT-04.invariant: All relationship reference mutations (Collection object/child link/unlink, Object.parent, matrix_parent_inverse parent binding, Constraint.target/pole_target) — whether initiated by Layer 4 in ACTIVE or restored by Layer 5 in ROLLING_BACK — must execute through Layer 3 Authorized Resource Operations and follow the 7-state operation log (PREPARED, APPLYING, APPLIED_VERIFIED, CONFIRMED, NO_EFFECT, REVERTED, RECOVERY_UNCERTAIN) and 10 legal transitions. Undo(m) requires Authorized(m) and Prepared(m) and IdentityVerified(m) and CausalEvidence(m) and NoExternalHarm(m). Distinguishes 5 relationship categories. Duplicate link on PRE_EXISTING_ORIGINAL transitions to NO_EFFECT with zero revocation rights. During rollback, APPLIED_VERIFIED and CONFIRMED transaction mutations must resolve to REVERTED via Layer 3; unproven states transition to RECOVERY_UNCERTAIN and preserve site.
CONTRACT-04.failure_condition: RNA assignment failure, invalid collection link, RNA pointer corruption during apply, or unprovable relationship state.
CONTRACT-04.exception_propagation: Fails back to Layer 1 with precise operational context; RECOVERY_UNCERTAIN causes Layer 5 rollback verification to fail.
CONTRACT-04.recovery_responsibility: Layer 5 inspects relationship logs and invokes Layer 3 to undo/restore verified transaction mutations to REVERTED while preserving pre-existing/external links.

CONTRACT-05.name: Constraint Configuration, Identity & Restoration
CONTRACT-05.invariant: Constraint deletion is strictly identity-based (reference + pointer) via Layer 3. Constraint target/pole_target bindings are relationship mutations executed via Layer 3 with 7-state logging, while numeric parameters (influence, pole_angle) are written by Layer 4 in ACTIVE and restored by Layer 5 in ROLLING_BACK. Transaction-created constraints are registered and deleted on rollback. External constraints are preserved with relative ordering intact.
CONTRACT-05.failure_condition: Constraint creation failure, same-name external collision, or destroyed original constraint.
CONTRACT-05.exception_propagation: Bubbles to Coordinator; verifier reports identity mismatch if original constraint destroyed.
CONTRACT-05.recovery_responsibility: Layer 5 deletes created constraints and restores constraint target relationships via Layer 3, and restores original numeric properties and relative ordering.

CONTRACT-06.name: Snapshot Integrity, Zero-Mutation Capture & FAILED-A Classification
CONTRACT-06.invariant: Snapshot captures deep immutable copies of all 4 controllers, 6 pose bones, constraints, and collection hierarchies with zero scene mutation. If snapshot read fails before any business write with proven zero mutations and intact Armature structure, Coordinator terminates transaction as FAILED-A without permanently quarantining the Armature.
CONTRACT-06.failure_condition: Unreadable property, missing bone, or view layer update failure during snapshotting.
CONTRACT-06.exception_propagation: Raises RuntimeError; Coordinator transitions transaction to FAILED (classified as FAILED-A if zero writes proven, or FAILED-C/D if structural corruption detected).
CONTRACT-06.recovery_responsibility: None required for FAILED-A (zero scene mutation occurred); structural corruption triggers FAILED-C/D isolation.

CONTRACT-07.name: Rollback Verification Symmetry & Categorized FAILED Session Isolation
CONTRACT-07.invariant: Rollback restoration and post-rollback verification are strictly symmetric (tolerance 1e-5, all modified relationship logs resolved to REVERTED or NO_EFFECT). Rollback execution failure (FAILED-B), verification mismatch (FAILED-C), or Armature death (FAILED-D) triggers immediate Layer 1 instruction to Layer 2 to record session isolation/tombstone under ArmatureSessionIdentityRecord. De-isolation requires Layer 5 category-specific evidence verification and Layer 1 Coordinator approval, logged in _DEISOLATION_AUDIT_LOG.
CONTRACT-07.failure_condition: Restoration error, pointer/reference identity mismatch, relationship log in RECOVERY_UNCERTAIN, or property diff > 1e-5.
CONTRACT-07.exception_propagation: Aggregates differences, raises compound RuntimeError, persists categorized session isolation or tombstone in Layer 2.
CONTRACT-07.recovery_responsibility: Layer 1 marks state FAILED; Layer 2 enforces session isolation for FAILED-B/C and tombstone for FAILED-D without falsely blocking new independent Armature identities.

CONTRACT-08.name: Irreversible Commit, Authorized DataBlock Cleanup & Coordinator Outcome Evaluation
CONTRACT-08.invariant: Commit crossing is irreversible; ordinary rollback is forbidden after COMMITTED. DataBlock deletion requires CanDelete(D, t) <=> AuthorizedCleanup(D, t) and IdentityVerified(D) and Users(D) == 0 and NoProtectedDependency(D). Type B DataBlocks without explicit grant and Type C DataBlocks are preserved as PRESERVED_NO_DELETE_AUTHORITY (not treated as failure). Layer 6 returns CleanupOutcome (SUCCESS/INCOMPLETE/FAILED) to Layer 1; Layer 6 NEVER independently modifies lifecycle state or deregisters gates.
CONTRACT-08.failure_condition: Obligatory cleanup deletion fails due to unexpected active user reference or Blender internal error.
CONTRACT-08.exception_propagation: Layer 6 returns CLEANUP_INCOMPLETE or CLEANUP_FAILED to Layer 1; Layer 1 transitions state to CLEANUP_PENDING and instructs Layer 2 to register gate.
CONTRACT-08.recovery_responsibility: Layer 1 dispatches idempotent retry via Layer 6 and alone authorizes Layer 2 gate deregistration upon CLEANUP_SUCCESS.

CONTRACT-09.name: Unidirectional Admission Gate & Coordinator-Authorized Gate Deregistration
CONTRACT-09.invariant: Layer 1 queries Layer 2 admission gate (_assert_arm_rig_cleanup_gate). Gate blocks new write transactions if the matching ArmatureSessionIdentityRecord has unresolved CLEANUP_PENDING or active FAILED-B/C isolation. Dead Armature tombstones (FAILED-D) cannot be cleared by pointer/name reuse, but do not block new Armatures with fresh session identities. Only Layer 1 Coordinator can authorize Layer 2 to clear CLEANUP_PENDING (after CLEANUP_SUCCESS) or lift FAILED isolation (after verified de-isolation report).
CONTRACT-09.failure_condition: Attempted write on Armature with unresolved CLEANUP_PENDING or active FAILED-B/C isolation, or attempt to spoof recovery of FAILED-D dead Armature.
CONTRACT-09.exception_propagation: Raises RuntimeError on write admission rejection with zero scene writes.
CONTRACT-09.recovery_responsibility: CLEANUP_PENDING resolved via Coordinator-supervised retry_pending_arm_rig_cleanup; FAILED-B/C/D resolved via Coordinator-approved de-isolation/tombstone governance.

CONTRACT-10.name: WBC / Arm IK Cross-Module Interface
CONTRACT-10.invariant: WBC relies on Arm IK for single-frame reachability feedback and zero-side-effect exception safety. Arm IK exceptions (including admission gate rejections and transaction failures) signal frame planning failure to WBC.
CONTRACT-10.failure_condition: Arm IK raises exception or returns unreachable target.
CONTRACT-10.exception_propagation: Propagates to WBC frame step; WBC handles kinematic fallback or aborts frame.
CONTRACT-10.recovery_responsibility: Arm IK guarantees clean rollback or explicit isolation; WBC manages trajectory plan.

CONTRACT-11.name: Bilateral Reset Atomic Transaction
CONTRACT-11.invariant: reset_arm_ik executes dual-arm reset within unified transaction. Each side reset sequentially updates: (1) Hand Controller, (2) Elbow Pole, (3) PoseBones neutral rotations, (4) Constraint Influences to 0.0, (5) Prebend Hint. Preflight failure guarantees zero writes. Mid-reset write failure triggers bilateral rollback. Nested reset failure reports rollback_only = True to outer Coordinator.
CONTRACT-11.failure_condition: Parent transform preflight failure, controller write error, influence write error, prebend write error, or depsgraph update error.
CONTRACT-11.exception_propagation: Preflight raises ValueError; write error triggers complete bilateral rollback and re-raises; nested error sets outer rollback_only.
CONTRACT-11.recovery_responsibility: Layer 5 restores both Left and Right arms to pre-reset snapshot state.

CONTRACT-12.name: External Resource, Unproven DataBlock & New Armature Isolation Protection
CONTRACT-12.invariant: External resources (unregistered objects/constraints/collections, Type B DataBlocks without explicit delete grant, Type C DataBlocks even with users == 0, and EXTERNAL_ADDED / OWNERSHIP_UNKNOWN relationships) are strictly protected from deletion or unlinking. Same-name collisions reject overwrite. Dead Armature tombstones (FAILED-D) never block newly created independent Armatures.
CONTRACT-12.failure_condition: External object occupies expected name, unprovable relationship encountered, or unauthorized DataBlock encountered during cleanup.
CONTRACT-12.exception_propagation: Collision/unknown relationship flags OWNERSHIP_UNPROVEN / RECOVERY_UNCERTAIN and aborts rollback; unauthorized DataBlock is safely retained as PRESERVED_NO_DELETE_AUTHORITY.
CONTRACT-12.recovery_responsibility: Halts destructive rollback on conflict; preserves unauthorized DataBlocks without false failure.

f4_reset_transaction_contract.architectural_position: Layer 4 Business API operating strictly within Layer 1 Transaction Coordinator.
core_invariants: Bilateral dual-arm atomicity: Left and Right arms belong to a single atomic transaction.
Zero-write preflight: Parent transform non-singularity verified before any scene write.
Unified snapshot: Baseline snapshot captured by Layer 1 covers both arms; no second snapshot.
Admission gate respect: Cannot execute writes if unresolved CLEANUP_PENDING or active FAILED-B/C isolation exists on Armature session identity.
Five-component reset sequence per side: Hand Controller, Elbow Pole, PoseBones neutral rotations, Constraint Influences, Prebend Hint.
execution_sequence: 1. Transaction Admission Check: Layer 1 queries Layer 2 gate via _assert_arm_rig_cleanup_gate(arm) checking ArmatureSessionIdentityRecord for CLEANUP_PENDING and FAILED-B/C isolation.

2. Parent Transform Preflight: Call compute_effective_parent_matrix() and validate_effective_parent_transform() for HandIK and ElbowPole controllers on both L and R sides. If any fails, raise ValueError with ZERO business writes (and mark outer_tx.rollback_only if nested).
4. Baseline Snapshot: Layer 5 captures immutable snapshot of both arms, controllers, constraints.

5. Left Arm Reset Writes: Sequentially update (1) HandIK.L transform, (2) ElbowPole.L transform, (3) upper_arm.L/forearm.L/hand.L Euler rotations to neutral (0,0,0), (4) ArmIK.L and HandRotation.L influences to 0.0, (5) apply Left Prebend Hint. (Observable fault boundary: reset_arm_ik_after_influence_l).

6. Right Arm Reset Writes: Sequentially update (1) HandIK.R transform, (2) ElbowPole.R transform, (3) upper_arm.R/forearm.R/hand.R Euler rotations to neutral (0,0,0), (4) ArmIK.R and HandRotation.R influences to 0.0, (5) apply Right Prebend Hint. (Observable fault boundary: reset_arm_ik_after_influence_r).
7. Commit Preparation: Depsgraph synchronization via _depsgraph_update(). (Observable fault boundary: reset_arm_ik_during_depsgraph_update).
8. Logical Commit: Coordinator transitions state to COMMITTED.
9. Post-Commit Cleanup: Coordinator invokes Layer 6 retry_cleanup(), evaluates returned CleanupOutcome, and authorizes Layer 2 state/gate update.

rules: If reset_arm_ik is invoked inside an outer transaction on the same Armature session identity, it reuses the outer context.
No early commit of the outer transaction is performed.
No independent post-commit cleanup is executed.
If reset_arm_ik fails during preflight or writes inside an outer transaction, it explicitly calls outer_tx.mark_rollback_only(reason).
Outer Coordinator checks tx.rollback_only at commit gate and rejects commit, forcing full rollback.
Preflight failure in nested reset raises ValueError without modifying scene, while guaranteeing outer transaction cannot silently commit.
If failure occurs on an obligatory cleanup item during Phase 3 cleanup after logical commit, ordinary rollback is forbidden.
Layer 6 returns CLEANUP_INCOMPLETE or CLEANUP_FAILED to Layer 1 Coordinator.
Coordinator transitions state to CLEANUP_PENDING and instructs Layer 2 to register the pending gate in _PENDING_ARM_RIG_CLEANUPS.
Subsequent writes on this Armature session identity are blocked until Coordinator-supervised retry_pending_arm_rig_cleanup receives CLEANUP_SUCCESS and authorizes Layer 2 gate deregistration.

        COMMITTING --> COMMITTED : _depsgraph_update() Passes (Commit Line Crossed)

        COMMITTING --> ROLLING_BACK : Depsgraph Update Failure

DECISION-A.decision: Refuse overwrite, protect existing scene graph. Automatic renaming of external objects is strictly forbidden. Ownership conflicts halt rollback and raise explicit errors.
DECISION-A.rationale: Prevents data loss or scene hierarchy scrambling in multi-asset or user-edited production environments.

DECISION-B.decision: Scoped to single-armature atomicity. Cross-armature two-phase commit (2PC) is excluded from this phase. Upper pipeline must orchestrate multi-character resets sequentially.
DECISION-B.rationale: Avoids over-engineering complex distributed transaction protocols before single-armature integrity is certified.

DECISION-C.topic: DataBlock Garbage Collection & Explicit Deletion Authorization Scope
DECISION-C.decision: Global bpy.data.orphans_purge() is strictly forbidden. Furthermore, Users(D) == 0 or deletion of an owning Object NEVER automatically grants DataBlock deletion authority. Physical deletion of a DataBlock D is permitted if and only if CanDelete(D, t) <=> AuthorizedCleanup(D, t) and IdentityVerified(D) and Users(D) == 0 and NoProtectedDependency(D) holds (covering Type A transaction-created DataBlocks and Type B pre-existing DataBlocks with an independent, explicit deletion grant). Pre-existing Type B DataBlocks without an explicit grant and all Type C external/unproven DataBlocks are preserved as PRESERVED_NO_DELETE_AUTHORITY.
DECISION-C.rationale: Zero user count in Blender only indicates absence of active references, not ownership. Preserving unauthorized DataBlocks prevents destroying pre-loaded assets, staging caches, or user datablocks while distinguishing legitimate preservation from obligatory cleanup failures.

unresolved_design_issues.topic: Depth of Isolation for Concurrent External Mutations During Active Transaction
unresolved_design_issues.scope_disposition: NON-BLOCKING BOUNDARY — Current headless pipeline executes single-threaded frame steps sequentially. If external handlers/drivers mutate resources mid-transaction, the draft safely halts destructive rollback via OWNERSHIP_UNPROVEN / RECOVERY_UNCERTAIN and isolates the Armature (FAILED-B/C). Active suppression of Blender depsgraph handlers is deferred to future multi-pipeline extensions.
unresolved_design_issues.description: Blender's Python environment executes on the main thread, but modal timers, background depsgraph handlers, or scene drivers can mutate scene data if triggered. The current architecture detects such interference during rollback/verification, transitions relationship logs to RECOVERY_UNCERTAIN, and isolates the Armature rather than performing unsafe deletions.

unresolved_design_issues.topic: Granularity of 7-State Relationship Mutation Logging for Dense Rigs
unresolved_design_issues.scope_disposition: NON-BLOCKING BOUNDARY — Scoped to standard 2-arm IK rig (4 controllers, 4 constraints, 1 collection, < 1 KB log overhead). High-density full-body rig scaling is out of scope for Task 10-B.
unresolved_design_issues.description: In the 7-state relationship operation log, recording per-operation reference/pointer pairs incurs negligible overhead for Arm IK. Compacted structures are only relevant if extended to hundreds of simultaneous constraints in future phases.

unresolved_design_issues.topic: Cross-Process Restart & Scene File Reload Persistence for FAILED Isolation
unresolved_design_issues.scope_disposition: NON-BLOCKING BOUNDARY — Current architecture explicitly bounds FAILED isolation to the active Blender process Python session (f2_state_transition_authority.persistent_failed_protection.isolation_scope_boundary) and forbids mutating Blender custom object properties during transactions. Cross-session persistence across .blend file saves/reloads is marked as a future unapproved extension.
unresolved_design_issues.description: Python in-memory registries (_ISOLATED_FAILED_ARMATURES, _MANAGED_ARMATURE_IDENTITIES) do not persist across Blender process termination or bpy.ops.wm.open_mainfile(). Persisting isolation across file reloads would require writing custom RNA properties onto Blender datablocks, which is intentionally prohibited in this phase to preserve the zero-mutation snapshot invariant.

All relationship reference restorations (Object.parent, matrix_parent_inverse parent binding, Constraint.target/pole_target, Collection membership/hierarchy) must invoke Layer 3 Authorized Resource Operations (_authorized_restore_relationship), which validates ownership/identity and updates the Layer 2 7-state relationship log to REVERTED or RECOVERY_UNCERTAIN.

AUDIT-BLK-03.resolution_summary: Added PROTECTION to the 5-value edge_type taxonomy (CALL, RESULT, STATE_READ, STATE_WRITE, PROTECTION). GATE-01.name: Layer Boundary Integrity
GATE-01.evidence: All 6 layers have mutually exclusive responsibilities and function lists in f2_layer_responsibilities and canonical_layer_permissions. Layer 4 and Layer 5 cannot bypass Layer 3 for relationship mutations or deletions; Layer 2 is purely passive; Layer 1 is the sole lifecycle and gate decision authority.

GATE-02.name: Call & Dependency DAG Integrity
GATE-02.evidence: All CALL edges in canonical_dependency_edges and f2_directed_dependency_graph form a strict DAG: WBC -> Layer 4 -> Layer 1 -> Layer 5 -> Layer 6 -> Layer 3 -> Layer 2. Upward edges are strictly stack return values (RESULT). PROTECTION edges point from Layer 5/6/3 to External Resources.

GATE-03.name: Resource Ownership Closure
GATE-03.evidence: All 18 operations in canonical_resource_operation_permissions enforce Delete(r) => OwnershipVerified(r, t) and IdentityVerified(r). Name inference and snapshot-diff inference are prohibited.

GATE-04.name: DataBlock Deletion Safety
GATE-04.evidence: CanDelete(D, t) <=> AuthorizedCleanup(D, t) and IdentityVerified(D) and Users(D) == 0 and NoProtectedDependency(D). Type B DataBlocks without independent explicit grant and Type C DataBlocks are preserved as PRESERVED_NO_DELETE_AUTHORITY without triggering CLEANUP_PENDING.

GATE-05.name: Relationship Log Closure
GATE-05.evidence: The 7-state Relationship Operation Log (PREPARED, APPLYING, APPLIED_VERIFIED, CONFIRMED, NO_EFFECT, REVERTED, RECOVERY_UNCERTAIN) and its 10 legal transitions are closed, separate from the 9-state transaction machine, and enforced across both forward mutations and rollback restorations via Layer 3.

GATE-06.name: Transaction State Machine Closure
GATE-06.evidence: All 9 transaction lifecycle states (CREATED, SNAPSHOTTING, ACTIVE, COMMITTING, COMMITTED, ROLLING_BACK, ROLLED_BACK, CLEANUP_PENDING, FAILED) and 12 canonical transitions in canonical_state_transitions.transaction_lifecycle_9_states have a single decision owner (Layer 1 Coordinator) and explicit guards.

GATE-07.name: FAILED Isolation & Recovery Closure
GATE-07.evidence: FAILED is categorized into FAILED-A (pre-write zero-mutation, non-quarantining), FAILED-B (rollback error), FAILED-C (verification mismatch), and FAILED-D (Armature RNA death tombstone). ArmatureSessionIdentityRecord prevents pointer/name spoofing while allowing new independent Armatures. De-isolation requires Layer 5 category-specific evidence verification and Layer 1 Coordinator approval.

GATE-08.name: Cleanup Authority Closure
GATE-08.evidence: Layer 6 updates only item-level progress flags and returns CleanupOutcome (RESULT) to Layer 1 Coordinator. Layer 6 never calls Layer 1 and never independently clears CLEANUP_PENDING or FAILED isolation.

GATE-09.name: Reset Atomicity Closure
GATE-09.evidence: f4_reset_transaction_contract, f4_reset_state_graph, and CONTRACT-11 define an isomorphic bilateral transaction flow with zero-write parent transform preflight, 5-step per-side reset (Hand, Pole, PoseBone Rotations, Constraint Influences, Prebend), nested rollback_only reporting, and post-commit cleanup.

GATE-10.name: Contract Set Equivalence
GATE-10.evidence: IDs_Registry == Unique(IDs_Impact) == IDs_Verification == {CONTRACT-01 .. CONTRACT-12}, with cardinality 12 and 100% aligned invariants across all three tables.

GATE-11.name: Verification Completeness
GATE-11.evidence: Every contract CONTRACT-01 .. CONTRACT-12 in f3_verification_requirements specifies normal_scenario, failure_scenario, external_shared_state_impact, invariant_to_verify, pass_criteria, fail_criteria, and verification_status = 'REQUIRED — NOT EXECUTED IN ARCHITECTURE PHASE'.

GATE-12.name: Governance & Honesty Compliance
GATE-12.evidence: metadata retains document_status = 'DRAFT_PENDING_INDEPENDENT_REVIEW', authoritative = false, implementation_verified = false, tests_executed_in_this_phase = false, and architecture_sync_update_permitted = false. Zero Python, test, or Markdown files were modified.

scope_exclusions.topic: Cross-Process Restart & .blend File Reload Isolation Persistence
scope_exclusions.rationale: FAILED-B/C/D isolation is bounded to the active Python interpreter session in memory (ARCH-ISSUE-03). Persisting isolation across file reloads would require mutating custom RNA properties on Blender datablocks, which is forbidden to preserve the zero-mutation snapshot invariant.
